Tamagotchi

Bandai’s egg-shaped virtual pet, sold as “the tiny pet from cyberspace”, made a pocket blobject out of a digital toy.

Source
V&A: Tamagotchi, B.239-1997
Creator
Aki Maita and Akihiro Yokoi, for Bandai
Made
1997 (V&A copy); first released in Japan on 23 November 1996 per Wikipedia
Styles
Y2K aesthetic (partial fit; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person), Kawaii (partial fit; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, cute, techno-optimistic
Evidence
Inspected the V&A photograph of object B.239-1997 (image 2006AE9151, 1200 × 1600), which shows the toy in its blister pack, in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A calls it “one of the biggest toy fads of the late-1990s” and describes an egg-shaped virtual pet “made from pink and green plastic” with an LCD screen and a metal chain, sealed in a clear bubble pack printed in five languages. V&A B.239-1997.

Wikipedia gives the Japanese release as 23 November 1996 and the United States release as 1 May 1997, and says nearly 40 million units had sold by spring 1998. Wikipedia: Tamagotchi.

Observed

  • The toy is a hot-pink egg with a lime-green face ring printed with numbers and a small square LCD in the center.
  • A silver bead chain loops from its top.
  • The blister pack is a clear plastic bubble with ribbed, rounded edges on a white card.
  • The card shows the Tamagotchi name in hand-drawn magenta capitals and three loose crayon-style drawings of an egg hatching; the slogan reads “The tiny pet from cyberspace”.

Why it belongs

The object, not the packaging, carries the style: a soft egg in candy colors that holds a digital creature. It predates the iMac, so it shows the candy blobject already in toys in 1996–97.

The crayon card art is a counter-example to the techno side of Y2K.
